title: The Dusk Count
hook: The lake had one rule for lifeguards: count the swimmers at sunset, and if there's one more... never count again.
lines: The lake had one rule for lifeguards. It was painted on the back of my chair.
Count the swimmers at sunset. If the number goes up by one... clear the water. Never count again.
All summer, the numbers matched. I figured it was an old joke for new guards.
Then, on the last night of August, I counted eleven heads bobbing in the dark water.
I blew the whistle. Everyone swam in, laughing, complaining about the cold.
Eleven people stood dripping on the sand.
Out past the rope, one dark head stayed above the water... perfectly still.
It didn't swim. It didn't sink. It just watched me.
Then it slipped under... without a single ripple.
And I broke the rule. I counted the beach one more time.
Eleven of them were shivering in the cold night air.
One of them wasn't. It just smiled at me... and asked for a ride home.
